reviewers.summary: The entry is mostly sound, but it has several problems. The "not used in continuous tenses" code sits in the patterns list. The "remain in a state" subsense does not narrow its parent sense. The quotative "go" subsense is in the same sense group as "make a sound". The be-going-to sense is ordered last. The "go for" and "the same goes for" uses are missing. The come/go and gone/been facts are repeated across many fields. Several phrase explanations restate their definitions, and a few examples are British or fit their definitions poorly.
The entry is well-structured and accurate, with no issues found.
